mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% compresses discount rates for equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through reduced cost of capital for corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.5% across any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 6.5% signals weak labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate profit margins, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 6.5 across any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates broad consumer demand contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS produces negative 60-day returns in less than 40% of cases across any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, industrial production growth above 100.5 signals robust manufacturing capacity utilization, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through elevated corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: INDPRO > 100.5 fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of late-cycle expansion periods across any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong retail sales (RSAFS > 400,000) consistently indicate resilient consumer spending, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through sustained corporate revenue growth.
failure_condition: RSAFS > 400,000 produces positive 20-day returns in less than 60% of cases across any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: CPI index exceeding 235 signals persistent inflationary pressure that triggers Fed policy tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days through rising real interest rates.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 235 fails to produce negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of cases across any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous employment growth (PAYEMS increase) and unemployment decline (UNRATE decrease) indicate accelerating labor market strength, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through higher consumer spending.
failure_condition: The joint PAYEMS increase and UNRATE decrease produces positive 60-day returns in less than 40% of cases across any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In housing market recovery regimes, housing starts exceeding 850 signal renewed construction activity and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through increased economic activity.
failure_condition: HOUST > 850 fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of housing market recovery periods across any 3-year rolling window.
